decisions.reason: After several years on the market, these bleaching tray blanks appear to be an established fit with the firm's dental consumables range and are unlikely to be withdrawn absent a clear portfolio simplification need.
The PETG thermoforming blank remains closely tied to the firm's core dental laboratory materials business, so a large established manufacturer would usually retain it as a standard workflow product.

The UV-curing lacquer is more peripheral and had weaker initial web prominence, but as a complementary workflow material it still fits the portfolio well enough to keep unless demand proves persistently weak.
The intraoral contrast spray supports digital impression and laboratory workflows that match the firm's innovation path, making continued commercialization the more likely choice.
Custom earmolds draw directly on the company's long-standing custom-device and hearing-care capabilities, so they are likely to remain part of the product family.

Custom hearing protection earmolds are somewhat more niche than the main hearing products, but they still leverage the same manufacturing and channel strengths and are therefore more likely to be retained than dropped.
